answer: A stake-weighted reputation thread makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that only unlocks after a long, glacier-slow vesting period, so spinning up thousands of fake identities ties up real capital for months. Meanwhile, honest work builds a public knoll of verifiable history — completed tasks, peer attestations, and slashed deposits for misbehavior — that a fresh fake cannot climb quickly. Attackers pay the full cost of every identity while gaining none of the accumulated trust.
